newsitem.title: USA: Latin American debt off lows but still weaker.
newsitem.headline: Latin American debt off lows but still weaker.

text.p: Latin American debt prices rebounded slightly from the day's lows, aided by strength in the U.S. Treasury market, but emerging market sources said prices still remained weaker.

Pablo Goldberg, analyst at I.D.E.A., said the breakdown of U.S. durable goods and the home sales data allowed the yield on the U.S. Treasury long bond to come down giving room for some recovery in the Bradies. But he noted that the market was still down from yesterday's closing levels.
A slight rebound in the Mexcian peso from its lows also lent some support to the market.
At 1630 EDT/2030 GMT, Argentine FRBs were 1/8 lower ar 79-5/8 bid, Brazilian "C" bonds were one percentage point lower at 67-3/4 bid, and Mexican pars were 1/8 lower at 68-1/8 bid.

"There was heavy selling most of the day, however, we got a lift when the housing numbers came out showing some weakness in the market and the Treasury rallied," said a head trader of emerging markets at one major U.S. investment house.
The source noted, however, that most of Friday's selling was not from clients.
"There was no selling from clients at all. I think it was mostly professional selling, maybe some back-book liquidation," he said.

Russian loans suffered some of the biggest losses Friday in continued reaction to Thursday's news that the International Monetary Fund failed to reach a conclusion on whether to give Russia the latest tranche of a $10 billion three-year loan.
Vnesh dollar-denominated paper ended down 1-7/8 lower at 73-1/4 bid and Vnesh mark loans closed down 1-1/2 at 76-1/2 bid.
"The news in Russia is clearly not that good and the market is being very cautious," one trader said.
